audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 with 54.76% over 431 games. Aurora owns levels 1-6 because Conquering Sands is 14s at rank 1 costing 70 mana and Arise! only deploys at 525, so a shoved wave leaves Azir with nothing; the lane hands over at first item when his Q reaches 6s at rank 5 and the soldiers start holding ground.

Spikes track real numbers: Conquering Sands 14/12/10/8/6, Shifting Sands 22/20.5/19/17.5/16 at 1100 range, Emperor's Divide 120/105/90 casting at only 250. The chart's flip at row 5 matches the packet levelChart exactly, and spikes[2] correctly names first item as Aurora's last clean window.

The decisive interaction is stated exactly as Riot's text has it: Shifting Sands dashes to one of his Sand Soldiers, so with no soldier on the ground he cannot cast it at all, and if it hits an enemy champion the dash halts on the spot — which makes body-blocking it a real answer rather than a hope. The E's shield is accounted for in tradeBad. Soldier attacks damaging everyone in a line is also captured, with the right conclusion that hiding behind the wave does not help.
breakdown.cooldowns carries digits and the conditional that matters: Shifting Sands 22s rank 1 at 1100 range and unusable with no soldier out, Conquering Sands 14s rank 1 falling to 6s at rank 5.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] is titled 'Kill his soldier during your recast window' but its body describes Azir spending Shifting Sands early instead.
audit.why: Title/body mismatch. The body should explain why killing the soldier is the play — that the soldier is the dash target, so clearing it turns the 22s into dead time.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d rewritten to match its own title.

edits.before: Azir spends Shifting Sands early — that is 22 seconds at rank 1 with no escape.
edits.after: Soldiers are what his E dashes to — clear them and the 22s is dead time.

notes: Level chart is consistent across all three layers — full-layer phases[].side, content win[], and the packet levelChart all read Aurora on rows 0-4 and Azir on rows 5-6, with every why matching its verdict. No chart edits needed. packet.suspectNames flagged three names; all three are false positives — Emperor's Divide is Azir's correct R name in spikes[1] and wants.foe[1], and wants.you[2] on disk reads 'Step back in the moment Emperor's Divide has passed you', not 'Save Between Worlds'. The packet defect 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' is also stale: the page already sequences off the 22s Shifting Sands and the 14s Q in breakdown.trading, dosFull[0].d and report[9].t. UNVERIFIED and deliberately not written: the kit's terrain flag on Emperor's Divide implies the soldier wall blocks dashes, which would mean it can cut Aurora's Across the Veil hop and her R leap mid-flight. Riot's own R text says only that it knocks back and damages, so the blocking claim is unsourced and no edit asserts it — worth a decision from the user before a later pass adds it.
